title: Cloud
body:
Renting someone else's servers instead of owning them: compute, storage, and networking billed
by use, from AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud. Listed in [[Node.js]]'s pros because most cloud
environments support Node as a first-class runtime.

The part that matters for this course is what it changes about deployment. A cloud provider
gives you machines on demand, so a service that gets busy adds instances behind a
[[Load Balancer]] rather than being rebuilt on a bigger box. That only works because [[HTTP]]
is a [[Stateless Protocol]]: any instance can serve any request, since none of them remembers
anything about the last one. Statelessness is what makes horizontal scaling possible, and the
cloud is what makes it worth having.

The usual tiers, from most control to least: raw virtual machines, then containers, then
managed platforms, then *serverless* functions, where you upload a handler and never see a
machine at all. Node suits the last two well because it starts fast and one process serves
many concurrent requests. See [[Server Side]] and [[CDN]].
